minutes.headline: Conservation Commission fined a tree company over trees cut at 32 Brookview and signed four Reservoir Road compliance certificates.
minutes.summary: The remote meeting heard many wetlands hearings: negative determinations for a garage, a retaining wall, a shed, a deck and a dock, and a continuance of the 99 New Street revegetation hearing to August 5. Members split over whether an engineer's "general accordance" letter satisfied the regulation, then signed certificates of compliance for four Reservoir Road lots. The commission also voted a per-tree fine over unpermitted tree cutting at 32 Brookview.

public_comment.topic: Former owner of the lot across the street recalled an earlier hearing and a French drain under the driveway near 135 Gilcrest, saying he saw no issue with the garage.
Questioned the process on 99 New Street, argued the dock and stairs should be decided now, and said the lake association has no enforcement authority.
Attorney asked whether the 183 Island Road matter would be reached that night; later asked about the deed restriction.

decisions.decision: The 99 New Street hearing is continued to August 5, when the dock and stairs RDA and the revegetation plan are both to be heard, with a more detailed planting plan requested.
The deed restriction for 183 Island Road will go on the commission's cloud and agenda for full-commission discussion before it goes to the applicant.
The Reservoir Road certificates were taken out of order because the engineer had to leave.
No certificate of compliance for 649 Reservoir Road until a corrected as-built is received; likely August 5.
The commission will consider an extra workshop meeting.

what_happened.line: The commission voted a per-tree fine on the tree company over six trees cut at 32 Brookview; one member voted no.
Certificates of compliance were signed for four Reservoir Road lots (167, 155, 143 and 131), each by roll call.
The 99 New Street revegetation hearing was continued to August 5, with a more detailed planting plan requested.
Negative determinations were voted for the Gilcrest garage, the Flat Hill Road retaining wall and the Townsend Harbor Road sand project, which excluded the dock.
No certificate of compliance for 649 Reservoir Road will issue until a corrected as-built is received, likely August 5.

why_it_matters: Wetlands rulings and fines set what neighbors near lakes and streams may build or cut, and what a property owner owes when work is done without a permit.
A delayed certificate of compliance can hold up a home sale, since buyers in one case hold back money until it issues.
watch_next: August 5 hearings: 99 New Street dock, stairs and revegetation plan, and the 445 Townsend Harbor Road notice of intent.
The 183 Island Road deed restriction, which goes to full-commission discussion before it goes to the applicant.
